question: What is the primary focus of observational data collection in research?
explanation: Observation captures real-time actions and environmental contexts rather than relying on retrospective reports. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h1)

question: Why do nurse researchers choose observation over interviews for certain studies?

options.A: It is completely free of any observer bias
options.B: It requires no ethical approval from committees
options.C: It captures actual behavior rather than self-reports
options.D: It takes less time than analyzing questionnaires

explanation: People often report what they think they should do rather than what they actually do. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h1)

question: A researcher who watches a ward routine without joining in or interacting is performing what type of observation?
explanation: Non-participant observation involves watching from the outside without actively engaging in the setting. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h2)

question: Unstructured observation is most useful during which phase of a research project?
explanation: Unstructured methods help researchers explore a new setting and identify key variables before designing rigid tools. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h2)

question: What is the term for changes in human behavior caused by the awareness of being studied?
explanation: Participants often alter their natural actions when they realize an observer is watching them. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h3)

question: Why is negotiating entry with gatekeepers necessary before starting observation in a clinic?

options.A: It eliminates the need for patient consent forms
options.B: It secures official permission and builds trust
options.C: It prevents the researcher from feeling tired

explanation: Gatekeepers control access to the setting and their approval ensures the study proceeds ethically and legally. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h3)

question: Which tool is best suited for recording the exact frequency of a specific nursing action?
explanation: Checklists allow observers to quickly tick off predefined behaviors as they occur. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h4)

question: A nurse researcher wants to measure how well junior staff perform hand hygiene. Which tool should be used to grade the technique?
explanation: Rating scales allow the observer to score the quality or degree of compliance, not just whether it happened. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h4)

question: What is a major limitation of observational research?

options.A: It never requires ethical board approval
options.B: It does not reveal the motives behind behaviors
options.C: It relies entirely on patient memory recall
options.D: It is impossible to use in hospital wards

explanation: Watching someone act tells you what they did, but not why they chose to do it. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h5)

question: Why is observer bias a significant concern during data collection?

options.A: Hospital management will alter the final research report
options.B: Patients will always refuse to take part in the study
options.C: Personal expectations can distort how events are recorded
options.D: Statistical software cannot process qualitative notes

explanation: Observers may unintentionally see or record what they expect to see rather than actual events. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h5)

question: How can a researcher improve the reliability of observational data?

options.A: By relying solely on unrecorded mental memories
options.B: By training observers and using standardized tools
options.C: By hiding the study purpose from all hospital staff
options.D: By changing the recording format every single day

explanation: Standardized tools and proper training ensure that different observers record similar events consistently. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h6)

question: Why is covert observation generally discouraged in nursing research?

options.A: It takes too much time to set up equipment
options.B: It violates the principle of informed consent
options.C: It requires patients to pay for research costs
options.D: It produces data that cannot be analyzed

explanation: Watching people without their knowledge strips them of their right to choose whether to participate. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h6)
